title: विश्व शान्तिको मुहान लुम्बिनी ः प्राचीनता र विकास
nepali: प्राचीन मानवीय सभ्यतास्थलका रूपमा चिनिने नेपाल अत्यन्त महŒवपूर्ण देवभूमि हो । ब्रह्माण्ड रक्षक भगवानशिवको बासस्थानदेखि मानव मुक्ति–भुक्तिका आधार मानिएका देवस्थल एवं तीर्थस्थलहरूको प्रचुरता रहेकोनेपाल अनेकौं महापुरुषहरूको जन्मस्थल–क्रिडास्थल प्रमाणित भइसकेको छ । विश्व जगत्मा धार्मिक क्रान्तिशुरु भएर कन्फुसियस, लाओत्से, इम्पेडोक्लस आदि दार्शनिकहरूको जन्म भई मध्य र मध्यपूर्व एशिया तरंगितभएकै अवधिमा नेपालका भूमिपुत्र गौतम बुद्धले थालेको धार्मिक सुधार अभियानले नयाँ धर्म–दर्शन नै स्थापनागर्ने परिस्थिति विकास भयो । सार्वभौम धर्मका रूपमा स्थापित हिन्दू धर्ममा यौन देखि योगसम्म, व्याकरणदेखिसृष्टिसम्म, उत्पादनदेखि राष्ट्र हुँदै सभा, समिति, सौरमण्डल आदि सबैको सिद्धान्त रहेको स्थितिले गर्दा जतिपटक लय (विनास) भएपनि पञ्चतŒवमा विद्यमान त्रिगुण रहुन्जेल सृष्टिक्रम निरन्तर चलिरहने विश्वास व्याप्तथियो । ब्रह्मचर्य, गृहस्थ, वानप्रस्थ र सन्यास नामका चार आश्रमहरूको व्यवस्था गरिएको हिन्दू दर्शनलेब्रह्मचर्यालाई तपश्या अर्थात् ज्ञानको चरण र गृहस्थलाई उत्पादनको मुल केन्द्रसँगै वैदिक मान्यताको मियोनै ठानेको छ । भौतिकताभन्दा अध्यात्मको यात्राका रूपमा वानप्रस्थलाई मानेर सन्यासलाई लोभ–मोह छाडेरज्ञानको प्रशारण एवं लोककल्याणसँग जोडेको छ । यसप्रकार ज्ञान र उत्पादनलाई केन्द्रमा राखेको हिन्दू दर्शननिर्देशित वैदिक सनातनको केन्द्ररूपि नेपालमा शैव–शाक्त परम्परामा आधारित शक्ति साधना अर्थात् बलीपूजाकोसिद्धान्त अन्तर्गतका सबै संस्कार–संस्कृतिमा नारी अनिवार्य तŒव मान्ने धर्म–दर्शन प्रचलित थियो । प्रवृत्ति रनिवृत्ति गरी दुइवटा मार्ग रहेको समग्र दर्शन (वैदिक सनातन हिन्दू) अन्तर्गत संसारलाई नै महŒवपूर्ण केन्द्रमान्ने सांसारिक ज्ञानलाई प्रवृत्ति मार्गका रूपमा लिइन्छ भने असंसारिक अर्थात् आत्मा परमात्माको चिन्तनलाईमूल मानी संसारलाई मिथ्या ठान्ने मार्गलाई निवृत्ति मार्ग ठह¥याइएको छ । त्यसबाट सांसारिक जगत्माशक्तिशाली र सम्पन्न बन्ने होडबाजी र बलीपूजा लगायतका प्रवृत्तिबाट जाति–वर्ण, धनी–गरिबको विविधता रविभेदपूर्ण स्थिति, राज्य विस्तारको होडबाजी व्याप्त भएको स्थितिमा जन्मिएर सांसारिक जीवन अवलोकनबाटैएक्ल्याएर दुःखको जानकारी नै नपाउने गरि आमोद प्रमोदयुक्त विलाशि जीवनमै भुलाएर हुर्काइएका सिद्धार्थलेउनन्तिस वर्षको उमेरमा पुगेपछि मात्र अकस्मात दुःख, जीवन सङ्घर्ष, मृत्यू आदिबारे यथार्थ बोध गर्ने अवसरपाए । त्यसबाट भित्रैदेखि वैराग्य उत्पन्न भएको स्थितिमा माया–मोहको बन्धन त्यागेको सन्यासीलाई प्रशन्नदेखेको स्थितिमा माया–मोहको बन्धनबाट उम्कने निश्चय गरेका सिद्धार्थले घरबार त्यागेर ६ वर्षसम्म गरेकोअध्ययन–साधनापछि ज्ञान प्राप्त गरि बुद्ध भए । त्यसपछि निवृत्तिमार्ग अर्थात् संसारलाई अनित्य अर्थात् दुःखमयकष्टमय र मायाजालको कारण ठह¥याएका उनले मुक्त हुन आह्वान गर्दै पदार्थको गतिशिलतालाई नाशवानमानि मुक्तिका लागि अग्रसर हुन आह्वान गर्दै हिँडे । रिसले वैरभाव शान्त हुँदैन प्रेम भावले मात्र हुन्छ, मानिसविवेकी हुन आफ्नो मूर्खतालाई चिन्नु पर्दछ, जात र वर्गको भावना लिएर कहिल्यै मुक्ति पाइँदैन, स्वर्ग प्राप्तिकोमूल आधार नै अहिंशा र निर्वाण हुन् भन्दै चार आर्य सत्य बोध गरि आर्य अष्टाङ्ग मार्ग अनुशरणमा जोडदिए । हिंसा जन्य यज्ञ परम्परा रहेको समाजमा संघको अवधारणा ल्याएर हिंसा विरुद्ध उभिएका बुद्ध–जीवनदर्शनको थालनी, महŒव, विकासक्रममाथि केन्द्रित यो लेख राष्ट्रियताको सिद्धान्त–अवधारणामा आधारित रहेरतयार पारिएको छ । समय, स्रोत साधनको कारणले गर्दा द्वितीयक स्रोतसँगै इतिहास–संस्कृतिविद्देखि लुम्बिनीविकासमा संलग्न व्यक्तित्वहरूसँगका अन्तर्वार्तामा आधारित भएर तयार पारिएको यो लेखबाट बौद्ध जन्मस्थललुम्बिनीको विकासक्रम, महŒव र बौद्ध दर्शनको जानकारीमा सघाउ पुग्ने आशा गरिएको छ ।
american_english: Known as a site of ancient human civilization, Nepal is an extremely important land of the gods. From the dwelling place of Lord Shiva, guardian of the universe, to the abundance of holy places and shrines regarded as the basis of human liberation and worldly enjoyment, Nepal has already been proven to be the birthplace and realm of activity of numerous great personages. During the very period when a religious revolution began in the world with the birth of philosophers such as Confucius, Laozi, and Empedocles, stirring Central and West Asia, circumstances developed in which the religious reform campaign initiated by Nepal's native son Gautama Buddha established an entirely new religion and philosophy. Because Hinduism, established as a universal religion, contained doctrines spanning from sexuality to yoga, grammar to creation, and production to the nation through to assemblies, committees, and the solar system, the belief was prevalent that no matter how many times dissolution (destruction) occurred, the cycle of creation would continuously proceed so long as the three gunas existing in the five elements remained. Hindu philosophy, having established the four life stages named Brahmacharya, Grihastha, Vanaprastha, and Sannyasa, regarded Brahmacharya as penance, that is, the stage of knowledge, and Grihastha as the main center of production alongside being the central pivot of Vedic values. Treating Vanaprastha as a journey of spirituality rather than materiality, it linked Sannyasa with relinquishing greed and worldly attachment to focus on the dissemination of knowledge and public welfare. In this way, in Nepal, as the central focal point of Vedic Sanatana guided by Hindu philosophy that placed knowledge and production at its core, a religious philosophy was prevalent that considered woman an essential element in all rites and culture under the doctrine of Shakti Sadhana, namely sacrificial worship (bali puja) based on the Shaiva-Shakta tradition. Under the overall philosophy (Vedic Sanatana Hindu) possessing two paths, Pravritti and Nivritti, worldly knowledge that regards the worldly realm itself as an important center is understood as the path of Pravritti, whereas the path that takes otherworldly contemplation of the soul and the Supreme Soul as primary and regards the world as illusory is designated as the path of Nivritti. From that, born into a state where rivalries to become powerful and wealthy in the worldly sphere alongside tendencies like animal sacrifice fostered diversity and discrimination across caste, varna, rich, and poor, and where scrambles for territorial expansion were prevalent, Siddhartha—who was shielded from observing worldly life, kept completely unaware of suffering, and raised immersed in an entertaining, luxurious existence—obtained the opportunity to suddenly perceive the reality of suffering, life's struggles, death, and related matters only upon reaching the age of twenty-nine. With deep detachment arising from within, and upon observing a joyful ascetic who had severed the bonds of illusory attachment, Siddhartha resolved to escape the bonds of worldly infatuation, abandoned his household, and attained enlightenment to become the Buddha after six years of study and spiritual practice. Thereafter, having designated the path of renunciation (Nivritti Marga)—that is, having determined the world to be impermanent, painful, distressing, and a source of illusory entrapment—he traveled about calling upon people to be liberated and urging them to strive toward liberation by regarding the dynamism of matter as perishable. Declaring that enmity is not appeased by hatred but solely through love, that a person must recognize their own foolishness to become discerning, that liberation can never be attained while harboring notions of caste and class, and that non-violence and Nirvana are the core foundation for attaining heaven, he realized the Four Noble Truths and emphasized following the Noble Eightfold Path. Centered on the inception, significance, and developmental trajectory of the Buddha's life philosophy—which introduced the concept of the Sangha into a society marked by violent sacrificial rituals and stood firm against violence—this article was prepared based on the theoretical concepts of nationality. Prepared on account of time and resource constraints using secondary sources alongside interviews with individuals ranging from historians and cultural scholars to figures involved in the development of Lumbini, it is hoped that this article will help assist in understanding the development trajectory, significance, and Buddhist philosophy of Lumbini, the birthplace of the Buddha.
